inputs.text: The proposed changes to Cyprus’ surveillance law deserve serious scrutiny. Surveillance can be necessary to protect public order and national security, but removing judicial oversight risks putting too much power in the hands of the state without a proper check. Lawyers are raising concerns, and the bill is expected to come before the House plenum for a vote on Thursday. After a recent closed session, lawmakers should be able to explain clearly why weakening this safeguard is justified. A responsible government should protect both security and the rule of law.
